_note: Words for /behind-the-scenes. Add a log entry whenever the site changes. This page is public: describe ideas, never server names, addresses, keys, accounts, or settings.

log.title: Choosing the approach
log.text: Instead of building an upload system from scratch, keep photos in a library I already manage at home and send out copies.

log.title: Eight designs, three rounds
log.text: A collage that flies together won the first round and is still the opening of the site.

log.title: The first site goes up
log.text: The chosen design turned into a working site, with web copies in cloud storage.

log.title: Real albums, real photos
log.text: The route from home was connected end to end. Place names, automatic titles, and true aspect ratios followed the same evening.

log.title: Drift
log.text: Four new concepts, and one winner: scrolling walks you forward through every photo in 3D, with a timeline to drag and a camera mode dial on right-click.

log.title: Faster, and open to everyone
log.text: A full check for speed and for people using keyboards and screen readers. On a phone, the pause while the 3D walk loads dropped by two thirds.

log.title: Smoother on phones
log.text: Photos load into the walk one at a time, and the far ones are let go, so scrolling stays steady.

log.title: Behind the scenes
log.text: This page, tucked into the right-click menu. Around it: the welcome line dropped its mention of the night, the corridor's two walls moved closer together on computers, the closing words follow the last photo without a long dark pause, and on phones the timeline moved up within easy reach of a thumb.

log.title: Photos that come to you
log.text: Click a photo in the walk and it lifts out of its spot, straightens up, and floats towards you until it fills the screen. Close it and it drifts back to where it was hanging, with the gap it left filling again. Anyone whose device asks for less motion still sees photos open and close in place.
